title: Make the computer talk
hook: Write your first three programs with one word: print.

warmup.q: No Python yet, just a guess. A program is most like...
options: A recipe: steps written down in order
warmup.explain: A program is a list of steps in a text file. The computer follows them in order, like a cook follows a recipe.

warmup.q: A call sheet says 06:00 crew call, 07:00 first shot. Which happens first?
warmup.explain: Top line first. Python reads your code the same way: top to bottom, one line at a time.

warmup.q: The computer shows you a red error message. What does it mean?
options: It could not follow one line, and it is telling you which one
warmup.explain: An error is a note from Python: this line, this problem. Every programmer sees them all day. You read it, fix it, run again.

why.heading: A program is a recipe
why.text: A program is a list of instructions in plain text. **Python** is the cook that reads your instructions and does them. You write, Python does. That is all coding is.

why.heading: print makes it talk
why.text:
The first instruction to learn is `print`. It shows text on the screen:

`print("Hello")`

The word `print`, then round brackets, then your text inside quotes. You will use it every single day, because it is how a program shows you what it is doing.

why.heading: Text lives inside quotes
why.text: The quotes tell Python: this is text, show it exactly as it is. Without quotes, Python thinks `Hello` is the name of something and goes looking for it. Text in quotes has a name: a **string**.

why.heading: Top to bottom
why.text: Python does line 1, then line 2, then line 3. It never skips ahead. So the order of your lines is the order things appear on screen.

why.heading: Errors are notes, not failures
why.text: Miss a quote or a bracket and Python stops and tells you the line. That is not you failing. That is Python helping. Read the line number, look at that line, fix it, run again.

watch.intro: Tap Run. Three print lines, three lines on screen, same order.
explain: Each `print` shows its text, then moves to a new line.
The quotes are not shown. They only mark where the text starts and ends.
watch.break_it: Now break it on purpose: delete the last quote on line 2 so it reads `print("Camera)` and tap Run. Read the error. It names line 2. Put the quote back and run again.

tasks.title: Say hello
tasks.task: Write one line that shows exactly: `Hello, Matthew!`
tasks.starter: # Type your line under this one
hints: You need the word print, then round brackets, then the text in quotes.
The shape is print("your text here"). Check the comma and the exclamation mark.

tasks.title: Call sheet header
tasks.task:
The lines are in the wrong order and one is missing. Make it show these three lines, in this order:

`CALL SHEET`
`Shoot day 1 of 5`
`Crew call: 06:00`
tasks.solution:
print("CALL SHEET")
print("Shoot day 1 of 5")
print("Crew call: 06:00")
hints: Python reads top to bottom, so the line you want first must be on line 1.
Swap the two lines, then add a third print line at the bottom.
The third line is print("Crew call: 06:00"). Capital letters and spaces must match.

tests.expect:
CALL SHEET
Shoot day 1 of 5
Crew call: 06:00

tasks.title: Fix the three bugs
tasks.task:
Each line has one mistake. Tap Run, read the error, fix that line, run again. When all three are fixed it shows:

`Lights`
`Camera`
`Action`
hints: Python stops at the first error it finds. Fix the line it names, then run again to find the next one.
Look for: a missing closing quote, a capital letter where it should be small, and a missing closing bracket.
Line 1 needs a quote after Lights. Line 2 must start with a small p. Line 3 needs a ) at the end.

recap: A program is a list of steps. Python reads them top to bottom.
print("text") shows text on the screen.
Text goes inside quotes. Text in quotes is called a string.
An error names the line. Read it, fix it, run again.

words.meaning: Instructions in a text file that the computer follows.
The language you write in, and the tool that runs it.
The instruction that shows something on screen.
Python's note that it could not follow a line.
